findings.title: Same-day payer replacement leaves two primary coverages and Medicare assembly selects the wrong payer
findings.description: Replacing a rank-1 payer closes the previous row on the new row's effective-from date. The reader treats effective-to as inclusive, so both rank-1 rows are active on the transition date. Medicare assembly queries only Medicare FFS and returns it as primary without comparing other coverage kinds.
findings.rootCause: The write path and read path disagree on interval semantics, and the billing seam has no range-wide, cross-kind primary-payer resolver.
findings.expectedBehavior: Exactly one payer occupies a rank on any service date, and Medicare assembly rejects a range whenever Medicare FFS is not unambiguously primary throughout it.
findings.actualBehavior: The real M5 reader returned both Medicare and commercial rank-1 coverage on the transition date; the real M23 adapter returned medicarePrimary=true.
reproduction: Create an old rank-1 Medicare FFS row and replace it with a rank-1 commercial row effective 2026-01-15 through the current interval semantics.
Run activeCoverageOfKind for both kinds on 2026-01-15 under chartwarden_app.
Run buildM23PatientPayerAdapter().medicarePrimaryForRange for that date and observe medicarePrimary=true.
findings.impact: A claim can be assembled against Medicare when another payer is simultaneously recorded as primary, risking invalid claims, denials, rework, and an incorrect coverage identifier/MBI basis.
findings.securityOrRegulatoryImpact: Billing integrity and minimum-necessary payer disclosure are affected; this is not evidence of MAC acceptance or of an actual submitted bad claim.
findings.recommendation: Adopt non-overlapping half-open dates or close the old row one day before the replacement, enforce non-overlap at the database/service layer, and expose one M5 range resolver that considers every coverage kind and every date boundary.
regressionTests: Claim assembly refusal before any claim row is committed

limitations: Synthetic isolated database; no external MAC submission was attempted

findings.title: Production release and deploy bypass the repository's full CI workflow
findings.description: CI runs on pull requests only to fix/admission, while deploy.yml comments out its reusable full-CI verify job. Release needs only debounce and deploy needs only release.
findings.rootCause: Metered Actions cost control was implemented by disconnecting required verification rather than by retaining one debounced verification path.
findings.expectedBehavior: The debounced current-main commit must pass typecheck, lint, architecture, tests, and required live suites before any image is released or deployed.
findings.actualBehavior: A main commit can build, scan, sign, and deploy without the full code-quality and behavioral suite; the current commit's lint failure illustrates reachability.
reproduction: Inspect ci.yml pull_request branch filters.
Inspect deploy.yml and observe verify is commented out and release needs debounce.
Observe deploy needs release only.
findings.impact: Defects that local or full CI would catch can reach production in an otherwise successful signed release.
findings.securityOrRegulatoryImpact: Security, tenant-isolation, and billing regression suites are not mandatory release controls; code signing authenticates an artifact but does not establish correctness.
findings.recommendation: Restore one debounced workflow_call verify dependency for release, keep the quiet-window gate, and make deployment consume only the verified commit digest.
regressionTests: Workflow graph test that release needs verify
Negative fixture proving a lint/test failure prevents release

limitations: GitHub branch-protection settings were not accessible

findings.title: Repository lint gate fails with 1,113 diagnostics
findings.description: The actual non-mutating Biome command reported 1,108 errors and 5 warnings across 963 files, including accessibility, hook-dependency, unstable-key, suspicious-expression, import, and formatting diagnostics.
findings.rootCause: The repository has accumulated diagnostics while the only release path does not require lint to pass.
findings.expectedBehavior: The configured lint command exits zero on the releasable commit, with intentional suppressions documented and scoped.
reproduction: Run bun run lint from the baseline commit without fix mode.
Run Biome JSON reporter to aggregate category and severity.
findings.impact: Real correctness and accessibility signals are hidden inside bulk formatting/import debt, weakening the quality gate and increasing regression risk.
findings.securityOrRegulatoryImpact: No security or HIPAA breach was inferred from diagnostic count alone.
findings.recommendation: Separate mechanical formatting/import cleanup from behavioral diagnostics, fix correctness/a11y findings first, then make the restored release gate require zero unapproved diagnostics.
regressionTests: Biome JSON diagnostic count is zero or equals an explicit shrinking baseline

limitations: Individual diagnostics were counted, not each manually adjudicated as a product defect

findings.title: Portal bundle-size gate reports a false zero-byte pass
findings.description: The built HTML uses /portal/assets paths. The checker joins that path under dist/app, silently skips the nonexistent file, totals zero bytes, and passes.
findings.rootCause: The checker does not strip the configured base path and treats every missing discovered asset as ignorable.
findings.expectedBehavior: All eager assets referenced by index.html resolve inside the build output; a missing asset is a hard failure.
findings.actualBehavior: The checker printed 0.0 kB and passed although the entry JavaScript was 395.08 kB raw.
reproduction: Build the portal.
Run bun run --cwd apps/portal size:check --check.
Compare its zero-byte result with the Vite build asset output.
findings.impact: Portal performance regressions can bypass the stated budget with false confidence.
findings.recommendation: Resolve URLs relative to Vite base/outDir and fail if any discovered eager asset does not exist or if the measured set is empty.

findings.title: Web and admin production entry bundles exceed configured budgets
findings.description: The web entry measured 549.7 kB raw and admin 577.1 kB raw against 350 kB budgets; Vite also warned both entry chunks exceed 500 kB.
findings.rootCause: Large eager route/application graphs are not sufficiently split, and the failing budget is not a mandatory release gate.
findings.expectedBehavior: Each production entry stays within its declared budget or has a reviewed, evidence-backed new budget.
reproduction: Build web and admin production applications.
Run each package's size:check --check command.
findings.impact: Slower initial loads and update downloads affect field clinicians and low-bandwidth environments.
findings.securityOrRegulatoryImpact: No direct compliance violation was established.
findings.recommendation: Profile the eager dependency graph, split infrequently used modules/routes, and enforce the corrected size checks in CI.
regressionTests: Representative cold-load performance budget on constrained network

limitations: No browser timing or device CPU measurement was performed

findings.title: HOPE SFV rule rejects LPN/LVN despite current CMS guidance
findings.description: The service and ABAC backing rule hard-code RN/NP for SFV and state that CMS requires this restriction. CMS HOPE Guidance Manual v1.03 clarifies that an LPN/LVN may conduct and complete an SFV when the hospice determines that discipline is appropriate.
findings.rootCause: A superseded interpretation of CMS discipline guidance was encoded as a closed authorization set and described as a mandate.
findings.expectedBehavior: The application permits currently authorized disciplines according to a versioned agency policy while accurately distinguishing CMS guidance from local policy.
findings.actualBehavior: LPN/LVN is denied with M10_DISCIPLINE_NOT_PERMITTED regardless of hospice policy.
reproduction: Call isSfvAuthorDisciplineAllowed('LPN') or 'LVN'.
Observe false and the RN/NP-only service guard.
Compare with CMS HOPE Guidance Manual v1.03/change table effective 2026-10-01.
findings.impact: Hospices may be unable to assign an otherwise appropriate licensed staff member, causing avoidable workflow delay and manual workarounds.
findings.securityOrRegulatoryImpact: The code over-restricts rather than under-protects; this is an operational compliance/configuration defect, not a finding that HOPE data was improperly submitted.
findings.recommendation: Version the discipline policy by effective date, include LPN/LVN for SFV where agency policy permits, update ABAC/service tests, and correct the CMS attribution.
regressionTests: LPN/LVN SFV allowed under enabled policy

limitations: No CMS submission or agency policy was available

findings.title: Medicare claim wizard delays payer compatibility validation until final assembly
findings.description: After patient selection the wizard does not query the existing patient-payer endpoint. The first payer compatibility decision occurs only when all fields are submitted to claim assembly.
findings.rootCause: The UI relies exclusively on the authoritative mutation and has no non-mutating preflight model despite an existing payer read endpoint.
findings.expectedBehavior: Selecting a patient and date range shows payer eligibility early while final server validation remains authoritative.
findings.actualBehavior: A user can complete every input before receiving NON_MEDICARE_PRIMARY_PAYER. The entered form is preserved in process memory and the error mapping is actionable, so data loss was not confirmed.
reproduction: Select a patient whose primary payer is not Medicare.
Complete provider, date range, and type of bill.
Submit and observe payer rejection only after the final action.
findings.impact: Billing staff waste time and discover correctable coverage problems late in a high-frequency workflow.
findings.securityOrRegulatoryImpact: Final server enforcement remains present; this finding does not allege an authorization bypass.
findings.recommendation: Use the existing payer read API or a dedicated read-only preflight after patient/date selection; keep assembly authoritative and preserve the draft on all failures.
regressionTests: Final mutation still rejects stale/change-raced payer

findings.title: Critical browser workflows and accessibility surfaces remain unverified
findings.description: Static reporting shows only 26 of 211 static web screens E2E-reached. The route-walk axe test excludes 116 dynamic web screens, all 47 admin/portal screens, and manual keyboard/focus/zoom/screen-reader checks. The audit could not safely start the full seeded stack.
findings.rootCause: Coverage is concentrated in a static web route walk and a small set of workflow specs; multi-app and data-dependent routes need separate fixtures/configurations.
findings.expectedBehavior: Critical clinical, billing, authorization, admin, and portal paths have runnable positive, negative, recovery, and accessibility browser tests across representative viewports.
findings.actualBehavior: The repository reports the gaps, and this audit has no runtime browser evidence to close them.
reproduction: Run bun run e2e:coverage.
Review the zero-E2E list and not-measured section.
Attempting test:e2e requires a separately provisioned full stack and seeded data.
findings.impact: Navigation, browser integration, viewport, and assistive-technology defects can survive otherwise broad unit/live coverage.
findings.securityOrRegulatoryImpact: Accessibility conformance and end-user authorization behavior cannot be concluded from static/unit tests alone.
findings.recommendation: Provision an isolated E2E environment, add admin/portal projects and seeded dynamic-route fixtures, and perform the documented manual WCAG 2.2 AA review.

limitations: No isolated full application stack was available

findings.title: Docling worker image ignores its lockfile and overrides incompatible dependency bounds
findings.description: The production image copies only pyproject.toml, installs broad minimum ranges from live indexes, explicitly does not use uv.lock, and forces Pillow 13 with --no-deps against upstream packages declaring Pillow below 13.
findings.rootCause: Security patching was handled by ad hoc resolver overrides instead of a tested, locked dependency set.
findings.expectedBehavior: The exact reviewed Python graph is locked, installed deterministically, and compatibility-tested.
findings.actualBehavior: The same source can resolve different transitive versions over time and bypass declared dependency compatibility.
reproduction: Inspect Dockerfile COPY and pip install commands.
Compare with the present uv.lock and pyproject ranges.
findings.impact: Document parsing behavior and availability can change between rebuilds; incompatible image-library combinations can corrupt or fail extraction.
findings.securityOrRegulatoryImpact: Patient documents are processed by this component; nondeterministic dependencies enlarge supply-chain and parser attack risk.
findings.recommendation: Generate a reviewed CPU-specific lock, install with hash/lock enforcement, remove --no-deps once upstream bounds are compatible, and rebuild on an explicit update cadence.

limitations: Image rebuild hash reproducibility was not measured

findings.title: Docling worker unit tests are not executed by repository CI
findings.description: The service declares pytest tests, but the path-specific PR workflow only builds and scans the image. No root/CI pytest invocation was found.
findings.rootCause: The non-TypeScript service is outside the monorepo test orchestration and its workflow treats image construction/CVE scanning as sufficient.
findings.expectedBehavior: Docling tests and a representative parser corpus run before the image can release.
findings.actualBehavior: Source changes can pass the image gate without running pytest.
reproduction: Inspect pr-image-gate.yml.
Search workflow/root scripts for pytest and compare with services/docling-worker/tests.
findings.impact: Document parsing regressions can reach production undetected.
findings.securityOrRegulatoryImpact: Malformed-document defenses and PHI extraction behavior lack a mandatory behavioral gate.
findings.recommendation: Install the locked test extra and run pytest plus golden/malformed fixtures before image scan/release.

limitations: External CI outside the repository was not inspected

findings.title: Production infrastructure uses mutable image tags
findings.description: Postgres, Valkey, MinIO, and ClamAV use tags rather than immutable digests; MinIO uses latest. Application images are digest-verified, but these stateful/support images are outside that protection.
findings.rootCause: Supply-chain immutability was implemented for application images only.
findings.expectedBehavior: Every production image is pinned by digest and advanced through a tested update process.
findings.actualBehavior: A pull can retrieve different infrastructure bytes without a source/configuration change.
reproduction: Inspect image fields in deploy/production/compose.yml.
findings.impact: Unplanned upgrades can create outages, incompatibilities, or rollback ambiguity in stateful services.
findings.securityOrRegulatoryImpact: Weakens software supply-chain provenance for systems holding PHI.
findings.recommendation: Pin digests, record versions/SBOMs, and update through a restore-tested compatibility pipeline.
regressionTests: Compose policy rejects non-digest production images

limitations: Running host image digests were not accessible

findings.title: Single-host production services lack resource isolation
findings.description: Only ClamAV defines CPU/memory limits. Postgres, Valkey, MinIO, Docling, API, worker, and web share the host without declared bounds.
findings.rootCause: Capacity isolation is incomplete in the single-host Compose topology.
findings.expectedBehavior: Resource requests/limits and capacity alerts prevent one workload from starving clinical/API/data services.
findings.actualBehavior: Most services may consume host resources up to daemon/host limits.
reproduction: Inspect production Compose resource declarations; observe limits only on clamav.
findings.impact: OCR, queue bursts, or database pressure can cause correlated availability failure.
findings.securityOrRegulatoryImpact: Availability of electronic PHI is a HIPAA Security Rule concern, but actual host exhaustion was not load-tested.
findings.recommendation: Establish measured per-service budgets, reserve database capacity, add alerts, and validate under realistic burst/load tests.

limitations: Host sizing and runtime utilization were unavailable

findings.title: Repository evidence states production has no object-store backup or coordinated database/object snapshot
findings.description: The restore-drill artifact explicitly says production has no object-store backup, no DB/object coordination, and no PITR. The successful drill is demo-scale and M36-scoped; the architecture document says the restored-schema RLS smoke is not implemented.
findings.rootCause: A demonstrator restore mechanism was completed before production-grade coordinated backup, off-site object protection, PITR, and full-schema verification.
findings.expectedBehavior: Encrypted, off-site, coordinated backups cover database and all objects; scheduled full restore drills prove RPO/RTO, RLS, integrity, and application usability.
findings.actualBehavior: Repository evidence supports only a local demo restore and explicitly records missing production object backup.
reproduction: Read audit/restore-drill/m36-restore-drill.md backup method and scale.
Read the DR/BCP restore checklist gaps.
findings.impact: A storage or site failure can permanently lose patient documents or restore database rows whose objects are absent/inconsistent.
findings.securityOrRegulatoryImpact: HIPAA contingency-plan and availability/integrity safeguards require operational evidence; code review cannot certify compliance.
findings.recommendation: Implement versioned off-site object backups, WAL/PITR, coordinated snapshot markers, immutable retention, automated full-schema/RLS/object verification, and recurring witnessed drills.

limitations: Production backup platform and operator records were not directly accessible

findings.title: Clinical free-text drafts are stored as plaintext in sessionStorage during step-up
findings.description: The addendum editor can place structured clinical content and free text into JSON sessionStorage when step-up is required. Entries are scoped, short-lived, cleared on take/cancel, and global clearing is wired into sign-out/screen-lock draft clearing, but browser storage remains plaintext and script-readable.
findings.rootCause: Step-up navigation recovery uses Web Storage because component memory does not survive the redirect.
findings.expectedBehavior: PHI-bearing drafts are not persisted in script-readable browser storage, or are stored server-side/encrypted with narrowly scoped one-time references.
findings.actualBehavior: Draft content is serialized under wx.step-up-draft.* until consumed, expired/swept, cancelled, or session clearing runs.
reproduction: Enter addendum free text.
Trigger a step-up-required save.
Inspect the tab's sessionStorage before completing/cancelling the return.
findings.impact: An XSS or local browser/session compromise can read temporary clinical content; crash/tab restoration may extend exposure until cleanup executes.
findings.securityOrRegulatoryImpact: This increases the PHI exposure surface. It is not, by itself, proof of a HIPAA breach or missing overall risk analysis.
findings.recommendation: Prefer a server-side encrypted, expiring draft keyed by a one-time token; if retained, minimize PHI fields, enforce CSP/Trusted Types, bound storage synchronously, and document the risk decision.
regressionTests: No PHI value appears in Web Storage
Draft token expires and is one-time

findings.title: HOPE live suite has order-dependent cluster-role cleanup
findings.description: The suite uses a handwritten four-role list rather than LIVE_DROP_ROLES/dropLiveRoles. It failed after another live suite left a migration-created cluster role, then passed 13/13 after canonical cleanup and database recreation.
findings.rootCause: The live test predates or bypasses the repository's canonical cluster-role lifecycle helper.
findings.expectedBehavior: Every live suite cleans the complete canonical role set and is independent of execution order.
findings.actualBehavior: Suite success depends on cluster history.
reproduction: Run a suite that creates a role absent from the local ROLES array.
Run the HOPE foundation suite on the same cluster.
Observe role-related setup failure; clean canonical roles and rerun to pass.
findings.impact: CI can fail nondeterministically and obscure real HOPE regressions.
findings.recommendation: Replace the local reset implementation with resetPublicSchema/dropLiveRoles and add the file to the canonical-role enforcement test.
regressionTests: Run after every role-creating live suite
Static rejection of local ROLES arrays

verification.result: failed then passed after canonical cleanup

findings.title: M17 on-call rotation table lacks live-test evidence
findings.description: The generated status matrix identifies only 8 of 9 M17-owned tables by name in live tests; oncall_rotation_entry is the uncovered table.
findings.rootCause: M17 live database scenarios do not exercise or name the on-call rotation source table.
findings.expectedBehavior: Rotation CRUD, tenancy, overlap/concurrency, and roster effects execute against live PostgreSQL.
findings.actualBehavior: The generated evidence ratchet marks the table unproven.
reproduction: Run bun run status:matrix and inspect M17 live coverage.
Search live tests for oncall_rotation_entry.
findings.impact: Schema, RLS, or scheduling behavior can regress without a database-level test signal.
findings.securityOrRegulatoryImpact: Potential on-call availability impact; no runtime defect was reproduced.
findings.recommendation: Add a private-database live suite covering tenant isolation, effective scheduling, overlap, and deletion/history behavior.

verification.method: generated coverage report plus source search
limitations: Absence of name coverage does not prove the feature is broken

findings.title: Automatic rollback can restart old code after forward-only schema changes
findings.description: On a post-migration failure, restore_previous_release restores old image references and force-recreates old API/worker/web even when migrations were applied. It loudly warns that compatibility is not enforced, but the incompatible state has already been activated.
findings.rootCause: Migrations are forward-only and transactional per file, while automatic image rollback assumes every applied change is expand-compatible without a machine-enforced contract.
findings.expectedBehavior: A failed deployment never automatically starts code against an unverified schema; expand/contract compatibility is enforced or rollback requires an explicit operator gate.
findings.actualBehavior: Old containers are restarted against the new/partially advanced schema and the script exits after warning.
reproduction: Apply at least one migration in a release.
Cause provision or service-start failure after migration.
Observe restore_previous_release force-recreate the prior images and emit SCHEMA/CODE MISMATCH.
findings.impact: Core services may start in an unknown schema/code combination, causing outage, data errors, or failed recovery during the moment rollback is most needed.
findings.securityOrRegulatoryImpact: Availability and integrity of ePHI can be affected; no destructive production event was executed.
findings.recommendation: Enforce expand-only migrations for auto-deploy, add a schema compatibility marker understood by both versions, and stop for operator decision instead of restarting old code when compatibility is unknown.
regressionTests: Injected post-migration failure with additive migration
Injected incompatible migration must refuse automatic rollback
Partial multi-file migration failure recovery drill

limitations: No production-like destructive deployment was executed

findings.title: Generated and narrative readiness artifacts contradict current implementation state
findings.description: The repository guide calls M41 a placeholder while the generated matrix reports it implemented; the generated matrix reports M38 routes absent despite enriched routes; the Medicare E2E spec still says assembly is unconditionally unreachable although the real seam/live suite now executes.
findings.rootCause: Narrative comments and heuristic status signals were not updated atomically with implementation changes.
findings.expectedBehavior: Generated artifacts define measurable facts and narrative docs explain current limitations without contradicting them.
findings.actualBehavior: Auditors and engineers receive mutually incompatible readiness claims.
reproduction: Compare AGENTS.md M41 statement with the generated implementation matrix.
Compare M38 route status with OpenAPI coverage.
Compare billing.spec.ts header with current M23 live claim-assembly tests.
findings.impact: Work is misprioritized and real verification gaps can be mistaken for either implemented controls or obsolete blockers.
findings.securityOrRegulatoryImpact: No direct violation, but compliance evidence reliability is weakened.
findings.recommendation: Correct the narrative statements and improve status heuristics for headless/API modules; make stale implementation claims testable where possible.
